item.content:encoded:
Not a bad series 1 article, notwithstanding the pointless end note. Ultimately, though, this left me feeling cold. The shallowness of the symbolism and on the nose nature of the imagery made it very much come across as someone who had done a little reading on East Asian scroll painting, rather than an actual object that could exist. In the end, this reminded me of nothing so much as this rather stupid urban legend.

Just as an aside, this article could be improved somewhat by having it anticipate future conflicts, rather than simply describe existing ones. An ending of "the painting changed and now we are trying to decipher what it means" would be far more interesting than "lol too bad it can't be a decoration :)"

-1

item.content:encoded:
There is an inconsistency in the text as it currently stands.

In the main text:

SCP-800 was retrieved in January 1979 from an antiques shop in the city of █████, in the southeast of the Republic of Korea. The proprietor, one Mr ██-███ M███, claimed to have a 'magic' painting which altered its appearance over the years; at the time, it displayed its present appearance.

In Appendix 800-1:

800-9 (1975-1979): unknown style of painting resembling Khmer stone carving, [DATA EXPUNGED]
800-10 (1979): 15th century Ming Dynasty style, Chinese dragon flying over rice paddies. Presumably depicts the Sino-Vietnamese Border War.

So according tot he appendix SCP-800 did not display its present appearance at any time in 1979.

There seem to be two ways to fix this. Either the Doctor who purchased SCP-800 was interested in a Khmer war drawing for personal use or the picture changed to the present one in late 1978, following Vietnamese occupation of Cambodgia. However, the latter looks a bit forced, given that conflict in Cambodgia/Kampuchea continued in some form for another decade. So I guess I'd rather see the Doc have Khmer-related interests.

The last note at the end, in which the SCP Foundation accidentally North Korea is, in my opinion, a great addition to the article, especially since North Korea has such things as SCP-1427 kicking around. Simple in-line link here shouldn't go to far amiss. As such, I am recommending the following edits:

Changing this:

To date the first and only alteration testing carried out on SCP-800. On 22/5/20██, SCP-800 (in its current form of 800-12) was altered using ink and brush by a Foundation staff member experienced in modern reproduction of Joseon dynasty painting. Addition consisted of a quiver of arrows on back of uppermost figure wielding bow. No effects were initially noted apart from the fact that altered paint remained for an unusually long number of days. Three days later, on 25/5/20██, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea [DATA EXPUNGED]. It is unknown whether this event was connected to Experiment 800-1. However, further experimentation has been suspended indefinitely. SCP-800 was restored to its original state by Foundation staff.

To this:

To date the first and only alteration testing carried out on SCP-800. On 22/5/20██, SCP-800 (in its current form of 800-12) was altered using ink and brush by a Foundation staff member experienced in modern reproduction of Joseon dynasty painting. No effects were initially noted apart from the fact that altered paint remained for an unusually long number of days. Three days later, on 25/5/20██, the Democratic People's Republic of Korea [DATA EXPUNGED]. It is unknown whether this event was connected to Experiment 800-1. However, further experimentation has been suspended indefinitely. SCP-800 was restored to its original state by Foundation staff.

I know what you're saying about "self-fulfilling prophecies", but in this case it's more like a nicely decorated RSS feed (one that just happens to be able to make news as well as receive it).
